status: SPEC ONLY - no retraining run (torch wave pending)
objective: Measure the causal effect on unseen-author generalization of removing the two zero-aligned accounts (OpenSourceIntel 200 rows, ResistanceNewsNetwork 2 rows) from training.

row_filter.description: Drop every corpus row whose author_source is in EXCLUDED_ACCOUNTS. Test splits are unchanged: held-out authors are never in the exclusion set, so test rows are identical before/after.

code_hook.edit: After concatenating the four raw CSVs and deriving author_source, insert: EXCLUDED_ACCOUNTS = ["OpenSourceIntel", "ResistanceNewsNetwork"]; df = df[~df["author_source"].isin(EXCLUDED_ACCOUNTS)].reset_index(drop=True). Applies to train/val/test construction equally; test authors unaffected (IDF, MariaZakharova, BernieSanders and all 14 fresh authors are disjoint from the exclusion set).

splits.val_policy: unchanged from baseline runs (same split_data code path, seed 42)

models_and_variants.note: Rerun the exact baseline arms whose numbers this study reports, nothing else.

command_caveat: Seeds are hardcoded SEED=42 in both scripts (no CLI flag); keep them so. Keep the 3+14 held-out author sets identical. Record the exact invoked commands in the run log.

readouts.primary: per-held-out-author recall_true_narrative after removal minus baseline recall (same author, same arm)
readouts.interpretation_prior: Under the independence model, 62.2% of LOAO errors and 92.2% of fresh-author errors fall on audit-flagged (neutral+mismatched) rows, but only 4.9% (LOAO) / 6.5% (fresh) on strictly mismatched rows; the removal set itself is 202/16510 (1.22%) of the corpus and 0% of any held-out test set. Expect a small effect; a large recall swing would implicate training-composition sensitivity beyond these two accounts.

reproduction: python3 with pandas/numpy only, seed 42; recompute tables by joining confusion-matrix diagonals against label_quality_per_text account strata as done in this study.
